name: Keir Legree
occupation: General Manager, Savoy Studios; Founder, PlanXT.com

bio.statement: Legree's voters' pamphlet statement lists 30 years as general manager of Savoy Studios and founding PlanXT.
bio.excerpt: General Manager, Savoy Studios (30 years); Founder, PlanXT

bio.statement: Legree's pamphlet statement lists a high school diploma from Rex Putnam High School.
bio.excerpt: Rex Putnam High School, High School Diploma

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury describes Savoy Studios, which Legree manages, as a lighting and art glass studio.
bio.excerpt: Legree, 54, is the general manager of Savoy Studios, a lighting and art glass studio.

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Legree says he has a plan and the city needs to work on ending street homelessness.
positions.excerpt: I have a plan, we need to work on ending street homelessness.

positions.statement: Legree's pamphlet statement calls for hiring more police officers and 911 dispatchers to improve response times.
positions.excerpt: hiring more police officers and 911 dispatchers to improve response times

positions.statement: Legree's pamphlet statement says he will work to reduce infrastructure project costs and lower utility bills.
positions.excerpt: I will work to reduce ongoing infrastructure project costs and lower our bills

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Legree calls street homelessness Portland's most urgent problem.
positions.excerpt: Street homelessness is Portland’s most urgent problem, affecting just about every other issue we face.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Legree calls for a compassionate approach that expects progress in exchange for services and treatment.
positions.excerpt: We need a new approach that is compassionate but also expects progress in exchange for services and treatment.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Filing form used is the second amended AUD-120.
